pairs.question: Demus, id quod nullo modo fieri potest, idem ingenii studii doctrinae pessimo atque optimo viro: uter melior dicetur orator?
pairs.derivation: Question needs the preceding 'demus... pessimo atque optimo viro' clause to give 'uter' (which of the two) its referents, so the window starts there; the interrogative is 'uter melior dicetur orator?'. The answer stops at the first full stop after the direct reply 'Nimirum qui homo quoque melior.'; what follows ('Non igitur umquam malus idem homo et perfectus orator.') is the drawn conclusion, not the answer itself.

pairs.question: Nam hoc certe nemo dubitabit, omnem orationem id agere ut iudici quae proposita fuerint vera et honesta videantur. Vtrum igitur hoc facilius bonus vir persuadebit an malus?
pairs.answer: Bonus quidem et dicet saepius vera atque honesta.
pairs.derivation: The interrogative 'Vtrum igitur hoc facilius bonus vir persuadebit an malus?' needs the prior sentence to give 'hoc' its referent (making things seem true and honest to the judge), so the window opens there. The answer is the direct reply 'Bonus quidem...'; it ends at the first full stop, before section XII turns to the elaboration about exceptions ('Sed etiam si quando...').
